newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to probe missing German war compensation.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to probe missing German war compensation.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma has ordered a criminal investigation into how war compensation meant for victims of the Nazis during World War Two vanished from a struggling Kiev bank, his press service said on Tuesday.

At stake is 87 million marks ($51 million) from a 400 million mark German government grant administered by the bank and a special Ukrainian government fund called the National Foundation for Understanding and Reconciliation.

"Violations of Ukrainian law by managers of the foundation and Gradobank were discovered during checks. In connection with this, a criminal case has been launched," Kuchma's press service said in a statement.
The money, received from Bonn in 1994, was frozen without explanation late last year by Gradobank, one of Ukraine's top five banks by founding capital, the statement said.
The General Prosecutor's office and Finance Ministry are carrying out the orders on behalf of the president, it said.

Last week the government made arrangements with Bank Ukraina, the biggest in the former Soviet republic, to sell Treasury bills in order to raise cash to make up the shortfall in compensation payments caused by the troubles at Gradobank.

The central bank took Gradobank under its control last year after it "found itself in a difficult financial situation and...was unable to make further compensation payments," central bank spokesman Dmytro Rikberg said. $ = 1.6950 marks
